title: Spider-Man: The Videogame (Japan)
input_profile_note: 1 = World wiring (MAME's ga2 / spidman input definition): Coin 1 on SERVICE12 bit 2, Coin 2 on bit 3, Start 1 / 2 on bits 4 / 5
expected_sums_source: checksums of the slot files built privately from this ROM set (not ROM data); band off, not consumed
hiscore_note: the same block as the World set: MAME's public hiscore.dat lists one entry for spidman, spidmanj and spidmanu. Own tag, so a save of another set is never restored into this one. If the block were wrong the markers would never be seen and the engine would stay idle
coin_chute_note: COIN ASSIGNMENTS > COIN CHUTE TYPE is EEPROM word 8 bits 15:8 (0x00 = COMMON, 0xFF = INDIVIDUAL; bit 8 read); CABINET TYPE is word 8 bits 7:0 (0 = 2P, 1 = 3P, 2 = 4P). Measured 2026-11-25 by changing the setting in the game's own test menu and diffing the saved EEPROM; the three regional sets run the same program (their saves are byte-identical). The core routes the coin inputs from this bit
cabinet_note: GAME ASSIGNMENTS > CABINET TYPE is EEPROM word 8 bits 1:0 of its low byte (0 = 2P, 1 = 3P, 2 = 4P; menu-written saves). With INDIVIDUAL chutes the game counts its coin lines (8255 PC b3, PC b2, SERVICE12 b3, SERVICE12 b2) by cabinet type exactly as Golden Axe: an N-player cabinet counts the last N for players 1..N (measured 2026-11-26, rel_derive.py CB); the core reads this field to route the coins
